title: How heavy can each sea animal get?
prompt: Place each one by the upper weight NOAA reports.

items.label: Jonah crab
items.fact: Jonah crab was once mainly lobster-fishery bycatch before becoming a targeted fishery.

items.label: Spotted seal
items.fact: Adult spotted seals are listed at 140 to 250 pounds and usually forage over the continental shelf.

items.label: Narwhal
items.fact: NOAA lists narwhals at 1,760 to 3,530 pounds, while newborn calves weigh about 176 pounds.

items.label: Cuvier's beaked whale
items.fact: Cuvier's beaked whales can weigh up to 6,800 pounds and have been recorded diving nearly two miles deep.

items.label: North Atlantic right whale
items.fact: North Atlantic right whales can weigh up to 140,000 pounds and feed by straining tiny crustaceans through baleen.

items.label: Blue whale
items.fact: The biggest blue whales can eat up to six tons of krill in a day.
